newsitem.title: GERMANY: Union, employers approve Lower Saxony wage deal.
newsitem.headline: Union, employers approve Lower Saxony wage deal.

text.p: The IG Metall trade union and the Gesamtmetall employers federation on Thursday gave their blessing to a pay deal struck for industrial workers in Lower Saxony guaranteeing full sick pay entitlements.
An IG Metall spokesman said that the union's wage committee had approved the deal -- which ignores government legislation enabling cuts in sick pay benefits to 80 percent of wages from 100 percent.
The Gesamtmetall employers federation also rubber stamped the two-year deal, which was struck early on Thursday after 14-hours of talks covering 90,000 workers.
Wages will rise 1.5 percent from next April and by 2.5 percent a year later. Year-end bonuses will be cut, resulting in a small overall rise in costs to employers.
Union chiefs hailed the agreement as a vindication of their industrial action against the sick pay cuts which has hit Germany's metal and engineering sector in recent months.
